howTo.label: How it works
howTo.title: Create random teams in four quick steps

steps.title: Paste names
steps.description: Add students, teammates, players, guests, or participants one per line or separated by commas.

steps.title: Choose the split
steps.description: Set a fixed number of groups or a preferred number of people per group.

steps.title: Generate and review
steps.description: Create a randomized assignment sheet, then reshuffle if the first draft is not a practical fit.

steps.title: Share the result
steps.description: Copy plain text, download a spreadsheet-friendly CSV, or print the current assignment sheet.

guides.title: Choosing number of groups or people per group
paragraphs: Number of groups is best when the room already has a fixed setup: six tables, four breakout rooms, three debate teams, or five event stations. The generator keeps that group count and spreads names across it.
People per group is best for pairs, trios, lab partners, workshop discussions, or game teams. Enter the preferred size and the tool creates as many groups as the roster needs.

guides.title: How the assignment sheet is created
paragraphs: The tool shuffles the current roster, then fills groups according to the selected split method. When the list does not divide evenly, extra names are spread across groups one at a time.
Use Reshuffle to keep the roster and settings while producing another random arrangement.

guides.title: Review checklist and limits
paragraphs: Random groups are a useful first draft, but the tool cannot know who is absent or which participants need a different assignment.
points: Check attendance before printing or sharing the final list.
Move names manually when skill level, accessibility, language, or conflict constraints matter.
Review sensitive participant information before displaying it on a shared screen.

guides.title: Exporting and sharing groups
paragraphs: Copy Results is best for chat, email, slides, or a shared document. Download CSV is better for a spreadsheet, attendance tracker, seating plan, or lesson plan.
The normal workflow does not require an account or upload step. The working roster is handled in your current browser page.

items.question: Can I choose the number of groups?
items.answer: Yes. Select Number of groups and enter the group count. The tool splits the roster across that many random groups.

items.question: Can I choose people per group?
items.answer: Yes. Select People per group and enter the preferred size. The page creates the number of groups needed for that roster.

items.question: How are uneven lists handled?
items.answer: Extra names are distributed one at a time, so final group sizes differ by no more than one in group-count mode.

items.question: Can I copy or download the groups?
items.answer: Yes. Copy Results creates plain text, while Download CSV creates a spreadsheet-friendly file with group, position, and name.

items.question: Does the tool upload my names?
items.answer: No account or upload step is used for the generator. The working roster stays in the current browser page.

items.question: Can I use it as a classroom group generator?
items.answer: Yes. It can help with class activities, project teams, lab pairs, or seating changes, provided you review the final assignments.
